name: IgG4-related mediastinitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Comprehensive Diagnostic Criteria for IgG4-Related Disease

criteria.description: Characteristic histopathological features including dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, storiform fibrosis, and obliterative phlebitis
Elevated number of IgG4-positive plasma cells (>10 per high power field) and IgG4/IgG ratio >40%
Imaging evidence of mediastinal soft tissue mass or fibrosis consistent with IgG4-related disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic features plus elevated IgG4-positive plasma cells; serum IgG4 elevation and imaging findings support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of malignancy and infectious causes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fibrosing mediastinal mass with storiform fibrosis
searchTerms: fibrous mass in chest with storiform pattern
mediastinal fibrosing tumor with whorled fibrosis
fibrosing mediastinal lesion with characteristic fibrosis
inflammation causing vein closure in chest

common.symptomName: Progressive dyspnea due to mediastinal fibrosis
common.notes: Resulting from airway or vascular compression
searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath from chest scarring
progressive breathing difficulty due to chest fibrosis

occasional.notes: Due to venous obstruction by fibrosis

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: voice changes due to recurrent laryngeal nerve
trouble swallowing due to food pipe blockage

imaging: CT or MRI showing mediastinal soft tissue mass or fibrosis
FDG-PET may show increased uptake in affected areas
other: Histopathology demonstrating lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis, and abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with prior histoplasmosis or tuberculosis
Presence of malignant lymphoid cells on biopsy
Absence of storiform fibrosis and obliterative phlebitis
No significant IgG4 plasma cell infiltration
Systemic granulomatous disease with multi-organ involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of mediastinal mass causing airway obstruction
Signs of superior vena cava syndrome
Unexplained elevated serum IgG4 with mediastinal fibrosis
references: Stone JH, Zen Y, Deshpande V. IgG4-related disease. N Engl J Med. 2012 Feb 9;366(6):539-51.

Umehara H, Okazaki K, Nakamura T, et al. Current approach to the diagnosis of IgG4-related disease - Combination of comprehensive diagnostic criteria and organ-specific criteria. Mod Rheumatol. 2017;27(3):381-391.
Cheuk W, Chan JK. IgG4-related sclerosing disease: a critical appraisal of an evolving clinicopathologic entity. Adv Anat Pathol. 2010 May;17(3):303-32.
